title: Tune NCCL streams, kernel scheduling, and KV-cache/continuous-batching for multi-GPU tensor-parallel collectives
author: Rohit Patel
description: Motivation: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were seeing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local kernel execution under real traffic shapes (short sequences with intermittent long tails). This PR tunes NCCL stream priorities, makes kernel scheduling more opportunistic, and removes contention in the KV-cache/continuous-batching path to improve comm/compute overlap and end-to-end throughput/latency. Changes are conservative: runtime behavior is behind a start-up flag and falls back to previous scheduling when we detect regressions. The description below summarizes design, implementation notes, and benchmark results.
commits: Initial tuning prototype (kernel scheduling + stream priorities); remove global KV-cache lock, add per-shard KV-cache mutex + lock-free fast-path; introduce priority stream group for NCCL collectives; opportunistic kernel enqueue when comm stream is blocking; add continuous-batching backpressure metric and adaptive batch window; add tests and microbenchmarks; update docs and feature flag; fix reviewer feedback on error handling and metrics naming.

release_notes: Performance: Improve multi-GPU tensor-parallel throughput and latency by tuning NCCL stream priorities, opportunistic kernel scheduling, and reducing KV-cache contention. Observed improvements: 12-18% throughput uplift on TP-8/TP-16 configs for short-sequence workloads and 8-14% P99 latency reduction in our internal benchmarks. Feature guarded by runtime flag; rollout will be gradual.
additional_context: Benchmarks were run on c5g-like internal clusters: TP-8 and TP-16 configs with a mix of short (<=128) and long (<=1024) sequences. Microbench harness (tests/perf/tp_nccl_overlap_bench.py) includes a noise budget to ensure statistical significance. Observability: added 'comm_compute_overlap_pct' and 'kvcache_fastpath_rate' metrics and dashboards. Compatibility: falls back to previous scheduling on NCCL errors and can be disabled via REDWOOD_TP_SCHED_V2=false.
notes_for_ops: When enabling in Dedicated or Private, monitor comm_compute_overlap_pct and queue_latency_ms. If overlap drops below baseline, flip feature flag off for the affected pool. Canary rollout schedule: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over three days if no regressions.
